newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed in moderate trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in moderate trade on Monday with the market largely focused on Tuesday's weekly T-bill auction amid an absence of significant economic news, dealers said.

"It's just a little bit of an adjustment here before we go through that supply cycle again," said Doug Sannuto, director of Canada cash markets with Bank of Montreal. "We'll certainly be trading in a narrow range. I don't see anything immediate here that's going to change the current rate structure."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 2.84 percent from 2.85 percent at Friday's close.
The Bank of Canada on Tuesday will auction C$5.1 billion in three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills even as C$5.9 billion in T-bills come due.
"It's really very quiet this morning," said a trader with one bank-owned brokerage. "I think what's become fairly common lately is quiet Mondays, waiting for the tender."
Dealers noted the T-bill yield curve steepened slightly, with shorter-term T-bills firming as longer-term issues weakened.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.11 percent from 3.10 at Friday's close.
The one-year when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.46 percent from 3.45 percent.
The call loan rate or overnight lending rate traded at 3.0 percent, the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
